title: Elodie and the Salt
premise: Ines Galloway, a beast-speaker concealing her forbidden gift while keeping ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things, is handed a dying stranger's map to the Salt Gate — the drowned covenant between the human realm and the tide-born. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and shadowed by a disgraced warden named Corren, she discovers her gift is the key the covenant demands: a voice both realms can hear. To reforge it, someone must speak the binding words from inside the salt and never return, and Ines must choose between the duty she was raised to and the justice the drowned have been denied for a century. In the end she rewrites the covenant itself — not as sacrifice but as shared inheritance — paying with her voice above water and gaining a life below it, while Corren carries her ledger back to prove what the guild buried.
about_author: Tamsin Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime trade records before turning to fiction. They write quiet, salt-stained fantasies about people who keep dangerous books.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet Ines balancing the guild's impossible accounts by day and secretly listening to the harbor gulls by night, hiding a gift that once got her aunt executed. When a bleeding stranger collapses into the counting-house clutching a map of drowned places, he presses it into her hands with his last breath: 'The salt remembers who owes.' Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine shattering.

chapters.title: What the Gulls Refuse to Say
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The gulls go silent around her — a sign the tide-born know she holds the map. Guild enforcers arrive to inventory the dead man's effects, and Ines lies for the first time in her careful life, hiding the map in a ledger of debts. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of becoming a criminal in small, precise ways.

chapters.title: A Warden Out of Water
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. A disgraced covenant-warden, Corren has spent ten years drunk on the guilt of failing to stop the Salt Gate's breaking. Assigned to find the missing map, he tracks Ines instead of reporting her, sensing the truth in how the animals obey her. Emotional beat: weary cynicism cracking into reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Brine
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Following the map inland to a dried seabed village, Ines learns the covenant wasn't broken — it was sold; her own guild profited from the tide-born's enslavement after the breach. Corren catches up to her, and instead of arresting her, asks to read the ledger page. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Drowned Court
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Guided by a half-drowned messenger eel, they descend through the flooded mine-shafts to the tide-born court, where Ines's gift makes her audible at last. The court shows her the covenant's original terms: a speaker from each realm, bound in trust. Her ancestors' side simply stopped coming. Emotional beat: awe giving way to inherited shame.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The court offers mercy with teeth: reforge the covenant, or the tides take the coast towns within one moon. But the old rite requires a permanent sacrifice — a voice given wholly to the salt. Ines signs nothing and returns to the surface to find the guild has declared her a thief and put a price on her head. Emotional beat: cornered resolve.

chapters.title: The Reading of Accounts
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Corren turns himself in to buy time, trading his testimony of the guild's century-old fraud for Ines's escape — and is imprisoned for it. Ines, reading his seized journals, realizes he has loved the sea's silence longer than he ever loved his own honor. Emotional beat: love confessed sideways, through paper.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Counting-House
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines breaks into the guild vault during a storm to steal the original covenant deed, confronting the guildmaster who once signed her aunt's death warrant. She reads the true accounts aloud to the assembled clerks — justice outside any law — as the tide-born rise in the harbor behind her. Emotional beat: righteous fury made public and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Speaking of Salt
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the ruined gate, Ines begins the rite and discovers the sacrifice clause is a forgery added later — the covenant only ever required two willing voices speaking together. She and Corren bind themselves jointly, his oath of wardenship and her beast-speech meeting in the middle. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into partnership; the gate opens green and singing.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Salt
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue-like. The new covenant names the tide-born heirs to the shore and humans heirs to the deep, with Ines as living ledger-keeper between them — her voice now belonging to water, her words carried by every gull and eel. Corren ferries messages across the threshold; the guild answers to a higher accounting now. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed, love kept, home redefined.
